sections.h2: What does a seller need to know about Tattnall County's layout?
sections.html:
Tattnall is a farm-and-river county in southeast Georgia. Reidsville holds the courthouse and Glennville is the biggest town. Wikipedia shows it was created on December 5, 1801, named for Josiah Tattnall, and measures 488 square miles, of which 8.9 are water.

Three river basins split the land. The Ohoopee drains the west, the Canoochee takes the northeast strip between Cobbtown and east of Reidsville, and the Altamaha collects the southeast and southwest corners. Municipalities are Cobbtown, Collins, Glennville, Manassas and Reidsville, and Mendes is a census-designated place. U.S. 25 shares a roadway with U.S. 301, U.S. 280 runs with State Route 30, and eight counties touch the boundary: Candler, Evans, Liberty, Long, Wayne, Appling, Toombs and Emanuel.

The county's own website devotes pages to agriculture and the Vidalia onion. The Census Bureau recorded 25,520 residents in 2010 and 22,842 in 2020, a drop of 10.5%, and its July 2025 estimate is 24,376.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Tattnall County housing?
sections.html:
The middle value for an owned home is $140,000 across 2020-2024, and owners occupy 71.0% of occupied housing. That is higher than the $117,100 to $120,200 range for Talbot, Terrell and Sumter counties, while middle gross rent is a lower $699.

sections.h2: Which Tattnall County office is which?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner bills and collects from 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, with P.O. Box 920 for mail. The county's payment portal lists the phone as 912-557-6736 and the hours as 8 to 5 on weekdays.

  • Tax commissioner: collects ad valorem tax, mobile home, public utility and timber taxes, and sells vehicle tags.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: five people picked by the county commissioners, plus a chief appraiser who runs the staff.
  • Board of Equalization: named by the Grand Jury and hears disputes over assessor values.
  • County commissioners and school board: write the budgets that set the millage.

According to the county's general information page, the assessors, not the commissioner, take the returns in Tattnall. The same page notes that the state itself may levy no more than one fourth of a mill.

sections.h2: How do returns, homestead and special assessments work in Tattnall County?
sections.html:
Anyone owning taxable property on January 1 files a return from then until April 1. The first return renews itself at the previous year's final value, so later filings are needed only for new property, improvements or a different value you wish to declare.

Homestead is for the house you own and live in, and the paperwork goes to the assessors' office. The Board of Tax Assessors page gives April 1 as the deadline and says the county has no local homestead exemptions, only the statewide ones. The FAQ asks for applications before March 1, so filing early avoids a miss.

The county's FAQ outlines these use-based programs:

  • Preferential agricultural property: 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40, with a ten year commitment.
  • Conservation use: valued by current use for bona fide farm or forest land, also ten years.
  • Environmentally sensitive and residential transitional land: current-use value, applied for between January 2 and April 1.
  • Standing timber: untaxed until sold or cut, then taxed on its full fair market value.

If you list enrolled land, ask the assessors what the covenant requires of the next owner.

sections.h2: How do Tattnall County assessors arrive at a value?
sections.html:
Fair market value, in the county's words, is what a knowledgeable buyer would pay and a willing seller would accept in an arm's length sale, fixed as of January 1. The assessed figure is 40 percent of it, and each mill of tax equals $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

The FAQ names three approaches. The cost approach takes replacement cost less depreciation and adds land, the market approach compares sales of similar properties, and the income approach capitalizes net income on rental or commercial property. Equipment, machinery and fixtures are also assessed at 40 percent. A seller with a recent arm's length sale has the best evidence for the market approach, so keep the contract and settlement statement handy.

sections.h2: When does Tattnall County want its tax money?
sections.html:
Look at your bill. The state's fact sheet for Tattnall treats December 20 as the official date, allows a switch to December 1 or November 15 or to installments, and gives each taxpayer 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest begins.

The online portal offers a property tax option, and the office line is 912-557-6736. Mobile homes run on a separate state schedule, with a location permit due within 30 days of permanent placement and a return plus permit renewal from January 1 to April 1 each year.

One credit on the bill is not guaranteed. The Homeowners Tax Relief Grant appears only when the General Assembly funds it, and the county warns that taxes climb if the state money is missing. Ask what credit, if any, is printed on your current bill.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Tattnall County valuation?
sections.html:
After the assessors change a value, you have 45 days from the notice date to answer in writing. The county says a late appeal is invalid.

Your reasons must be taxability, uniformity or value. Dislike of the tax itself does not count. The assessors look first, and if they leave the number alone, the file moves to the Board of Equalization for a hearing, then to Tattnall County Superior Court if either side wants more. You may pick arbitration over the Board of Equalization when you file.

The county explains that assessors interpret the market and do not invent prices. If a recent contract differs from the county's number, bring that contract with your appeal.

sections.h2: What happens if Tattnall County tax stays unpaid?
sections.html:
The county has sold properties at the courthouse. One sale was held Tuesday, June 7, 2022, at 10 a.m. in the second-floor Commissioners Meeting room. A sale ends a long delinquency, so an owner with a back balance has choices well before that.

Request written payoffs for each year, and for a mobile home, confirm the decal and permit are paid. The county FAQ says tax is charged against whoever owns the property on January 1, and the closing statement is where you and the buyer divide the year. The title company then pays any earlier balance from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Tattnall County property tax?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner's office, 108 West Brazell St. in Reidsville, or through the county's online payment portal. The phone is 912-557-6736 and the office keeps hours of 8 to 5 on weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the homestead cutoff in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: April 1 per the Board of Tax Assessors page. The county FAQ mentions March 1, so file before March to be safe. The assessors' office takes the form.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to appeal in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date of the notice, in writing. Late appeals are invalid.

faqs.q: Does Tattnall County have its own homestead exemptions?
faqs.a: No. The Board of Tax Assessors page says none are offered locally, so owners apply for the statewide exemptions.

faqs.q: Is timber taxed in Tattnall County?
faqs.a: Yes, when it is sold or harvested. The tax uses 100 percent of fair market value, and the FAQ covers lump sum, unit price and owner harvest sales.
